newsitem.title: UK: EU grains lower, UK hammered by strong pound.
newsitem.headline: EU grains lower, UK hammered by strong pound.

text.p: UK grain prices were struck by Wednesday's interest rate hike and a strong pound sterling and bearish sentiment generally hung over European grains this week. Slack export prospects despite the European Commission's generous wheat subsidy last week and sliding benchmark Chicago futures fuelled the weak tone. Buyers had a wide selection of competitively-priced origins to chose from.
On export markets, French traders were frustrated by Argentina selling wheat aggressively to one of their biggest outlets, Algeria, despite the freight cost differential.
German grains were marked further down with little in the pipeline from eastern European buyers.
A significantly higher 13 Ecu export subsidy on soft wheat given by the EU last week was considered bullish, but traders said they expected volumes to remain under a tight rein.
"Weekly exports out of Brussels might get stuck in a 200,000 to 300,000 tonne range in the next few weeks," one said.
Sales of 150,000 tonnes of French wheat at the weekend at a price range of $146.5-$147 per tonne Fob heralded a new tussle with the Commission as these would require larger subsidies.
But the French domestic market ignored the sales and prices were a touch lower on nearby deliveries.
A surprise qurater-point rise in UK interest rates on Wednesday shaved one stg off domestic grain prices as the market responded to sterling's advance.
"Just like a rabbit chasing the snake, the market is basically monitoring sterling," said one trader.

Interest for barley was dwindling as compounders were shifting to wheat which is almost trading at level. Traders were waiting for clues from the EU's weekly tender on fresh allocations for a recent sale to Saudi Arabia.
German sellers were slowly succumbing to market pressure of rising supply but trading conditions stayed thin.
The Hamburg grain exchange lowered prices once again while in the fob Baltic export market, 12 percent material was quoted a few marks lower in a 285-290 mark range.
Barley prices headed lower in thin demand, raising prospects for large intervention offers across the Continent this season.
French maize was easier with the harvest now in full swing.
Maize declined sharply in Italy where warehouses were filled up with the newly gathered crop while producers seemed eager to put excess on the market at almost any price.
But one dealer saw some hope for a recovery.

"The current sharp drop in prices is only a temporary factor tied to the harvest. There have been contracts taken out on maize for delivery from January to June on the basis of 294,000 lire per tonne," the dealer said.
Otherwise, trade in cereals was thin with most prices lower.
"There is some trade to be found but it's like hunting for a needle in a haystack," one dealer said.
